title: On the First Christian Sabbath Eve
description: On the First Christian Sabbath Eve in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 56 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Introduction to Evening Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: On the first Chris-tian Sab-bath eve, When his dis-ci-ples met O'er his lost fel-low-ship to grieve, Nor knew the Scrip-ture yet,

lines: On the first Christian Sabbath eve,
O'er his lost fellowship to grieve,
Lo! in their midst his form was seen, —
The form in which he died;
Their Master's marred and wounded mien, —
His hands, his feet, his side.
Then were they glad their Lord to know,
And hailed him, yet with fear; —
Be in our midst; let faith rejoice
And make our spirits hear thy voice

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
